newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIUM PLANS TO RAISE WOMEN'S PENSION AGE - RADIO.
newsitem.headline: BELGIUM PLANS TO RAISE WOMEN'S PENSION AGE - RADIO.

text.p: The Belgian government plans to gradually raise the retirement age for women to 65 years from 60 now, Belgian BRTN radio said on Tuesday.
It said Pensions Minister Marcel Colla had drawn up a draft note proposing the retirement age for women be raised to 65 over a period of nine years to bring it in line with that for men.

Colla declined to comment on the note, but confirmed he was working on a pensions initiative. "In view of the ageing of the Belgian population and the need for legal equal rights in Europe (for men and women)...we will need to ask women to make an effort," he told BRTN.
The reform of the Belgian pension system is one of the top priorities of Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene's centre-left coalition government.
Cabinet ministers are currently drafting the 1997 budget, which is expected to contain about 100 billion francs worth of austerity measures.
